title: Container
wrapsNative: frame(maxWidth:) centred with a second frame(maxWidth: .infinity), padding(.horizontal, _:) by horizontalSizeClass, and containerRelativeFrame(_:count:span:spacing:alignment:)
summary: Centring page content at a maximum width with side gutters is a pair of frame modifiers and horizontal padding. Monarch ships nothing and documents the widths and gutters.
whenToUse: On screens that can be wide (iPad, landscape) to stop text and forms from stretching: cap the width at 704 points for reading and forms, 1152 for app pages or 1280 for dashboards, and pad by 16 points in a compact width and 24 in a regular width. Use containerRelativeFrame to size a view as a part of its container.
whenNotToUse: Inside List, Form and NavigationStack the system already applies margins and readable widths; do not add another container there.
api: func frame(minWidth: CGFloat? = nil, idealWidth: CGFloat? = nil, maxWidth: CGFloat? = nil, minHeight: CGFloat? = nil, idealHeight: CGFloat? = nil, maxHeight: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment = .center) -> some View
func containerRelativeFrame(_ axes: Axis.Set, count: Int, span: Int = 1, spacing: CGFloat, alignment: Alignment = .center) -> some View

states.name: compact width
states.description: 16-point gutters (theme.spacing.space4). The content fills the width.

states.name: regular width
states.description: 24-point gutters (theme.spacing.space6). The content stops at the maximum width and is centred.

platformNotes: The web's Container has sizes narrow (44rem, 704 points), content (72rem, 1152), wide (80rem, 1280) and full, and gutters of 16px that become 24px from 768px. The native tokens carry no width tokens, so the numbers are written in the app; the gutters are steps of the space scale, and the size class replaces the 768px breakpoint. Android uses widthIn(max:) and window size classes in the same way.
accessibility: Layout only: no element is added and the reading order does not change.
Leading and trailing padding follow the layout direction.
A capped width keeps lines readable on wide screens; at large Dynamic Type sizes the content still fills a compact width.
edgeCases: The maximum width here includes the gutters, as on the web, because the padding is applied before the frame.
containerRelativeFrame measures the nearest container: a ScrollView, a column of a split view or the window.
On macOS the size class is always regular.
